Alex Kim: Heads-up — DSAR for EU data coming in; legal needs deletion confirmation within 30d. Do we need an RBAC role change for the team that runs deletion so they can access KMS key metadata and audit logs? Any retention-exception window we should apply?

Priya Nair: For DSAR deletes we don't give raw KMS key access. We use the keystore service playbook to perform crypto ops. Engineers get `keystore:request` via a service principal, not direct key grants. Legal wants proof-of-deletion (signed receipts).

Jordan Lee: Can you paste the requester ID and affected datasets? If it's embeddings we must run vector-db purge + manifest update. RBAC proposal: create scoped role `dsar-deleter` with `audit.read` + `keystore.request` for the DSAR worker service account. No `kms:grant` or key material.

Maya Ortiz: Legal: requester is `subject-789` — want confirmation that all personal identifiers removed (names, emails, contact) and a verifiable artifact. We need proof artifacts within 14d ideally.

Alex Kim: Requester ID noted. Quick Q: how do we capture immutable audit trail without exposing PII to engineers? We must show proof of action to legal without exposing raw data.

Priya Nair: Proposed approach: generate a signed deletion receipt (sha256 of object id + timestamp + salt) and persist the receipt in the audit store. Provide hashed receipts to legal. Engineers never see PII unless a breakglass occurs. See playbook snippet below.

Priya Nair: ```bash
# generate receipt
OBJECT_ID="doc:subject-789"
NOW=$(date -u +%s)
SALT=$(openssl rand -hex 12)
HASH=$(echo -n "${OBJECT_ID}:${NOW}:${SALT}" | sha256sum | awk '{print $1}')
# persist receipt
curl -s -X POST https://audit.internal.redwood/api/receipts \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"receipt":"'$HASH'","action":"dsar_delete","actor":"service:dsar-worker","meta":{"requester":"subject-789"}}'
```

Jordan Lee: For audit aggregation use: `SELECT * FROM audit.events WHERE action='dsar_delete' AND receipt='{HASH}';` After proof generation move any minimal evidence to a retention-exception bucket `gdpr_evidence` with a short TTL. Ops should not have direct access to PII in that bucket; access audited and gated.

Sam (oncall): Recommend creating a retention-exception for evidence hold of 45d (legal review window). That requires approvals from Security + Legal and a ticket so we can automate TTL. I'll open the ticket.

incidents-bot: Created ticket INFRA-5421 for retention-exception request by @sam (link: https://jira.redwood.internal/browse/INFRA-5421)

Maya Ortiz: Legal approves 45d evidence hold for this DSAR only. Please ensure keys used for encryption are rotated or sealed after deletion and that access is sealed.

Alex Kim: Action items: 1) Jordan to create `dsar-deleter` role (audit.read, keystore.request) scoped to service account; 2) Priya to add receipt generation to dsar-worker and write to audit; 3) Sam to create INFRA-5421 and attach approvals; 4) Jordan to run purge plan and provide hashed receipts to Legal. Target: complete within 7d. @channel please ack. :lock:

Priya Nair: Ack

Jordan Lee: Ack — starting role and DB scripts now

Sam (oncall): Ack — will escalate if approval delays

Maya Ortiz: Ack from Legal

Alex Kim: Closing loop — if anyone needs to view PII for forensics we follow the legal+security breakglass process. Keep this thread updated with timestamps and receipts. :eyes:
